name: Shakti cerebellum: ERP signal below the inion ('undo' session)
summary: Murphy's one-coil Shakti session over the cerebellum, just below the bony ridge at the back of the head: 20 min of an event-related-potential (ERP) signal. The vendor calls the cerebellum a 'pleasure/orgasm center' and suggests cerebellar ERP to 'un-do unwanted effects' after sessions that used both the amygdala and the hippocampal signals.
setting: As an 'undo' session after sessions that used both the amygdala and hippocampal signals, or in series that alternate with series over other areas (vendor). Sit, or lie on your side, so the coil at the back of the head is not pressed.
schedule: Vendor: alternate cerebellar series with series over other areas. The vendor's general Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break.
notes: One coil at Iz, the 10-5 site on the inion: the vendor says to 'use the bony ridge at the back of your head', with the occipital lobes above the ridge and the cerebellum below it, and uses a one-coil headset, so seat the coil on or just below the ridge. Iz is an inference; I1 or I2 (a little to either side) and O9 or O10 (further out) are alternative sites. The other seven channels stay unused. A coil below the inion is hard to hold on a Velcro band, so check that it sits firmly and comfortably. The vendor's ERP file is proprietary and undescribed; this file uses the project's ERP construct (textbook P50, N100, P200, N200 and P300 components after Luck 2014: a 0.6-s pulse every 1.5 s, 1-ms points), not the Shakti file. The vendor's volume table (desktop sound card 90% for men and 58% for women; laptop or onboard sound 100% for both) sets sound-card levels, not a calibrated field. The default here is 1 µT; the table's lower desktop setting for women would mean about two-thirds of that. The vendor also allows the modulated 40 Hz signal here (murphy-shakti-cerebellum-erp-mod40). Its statement that 'cerebellar activation can attenuate limbic, particularly amygdaloid, activation' is a vendor claim, and the vendor calls the ERP signal untested. The vendor warns that 'excess cerebellar activation may lead to emotional flattening', so do not overuse it. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
